title: When the Echo Sings
premise: Juniper Underhill, a former insurance investigator hiding a decade-old secret aboard the colony ship Meridian, discovers that the colony's children are all dreaming the same dream — a song transmitted from the derelict first-generation vessel drifting in contested orbit, which both warring factions claim. The dream is an inheritance: a recorded consciousness of Meridian's original architect, who was Juniper's mother and whose death he helped cover up to protect the colony's fragile peace. As the children's shared dream begins synchronizing their behavior and the war fleets converge on the derelict, Juniper must decide whether to reveal his identity and deliver the architect's final message — a confession proving neither faction's founding claim is true. In the end, Juniper broadcasts the message through the children themselves, ending the war not with victory but with shared grief, and finally belonging to the community he spent ten years avoiding.
about_author: Bram Voss is the pen name of a former maritime insurance adjuster who traded harbor offices for writing science fiction about people who calculate risk for a living. Their work explores how institutions remember, and how individuals survive being forgotten by them.

chapters.title: Actuarial Grace
chapters.summary: Juniper Underhill processes a claim for a cargo hauler crushed by a docking accident that statistics say shouldn't happen three times in one year. Through his POV we learn he notices patterns others miss — and deliberately files this one as coincidence. Emotional beat: the practiced numbness of a man keeping his head down.

chapters.title: The Children Who Stopped Playing Different Games
chapters.summary: Teacher Odile Ferro watches forty children on the habitat ring abandon recess simultaneously and stand facing the same viewport, humming an identical melody no one taught them. Her POV establishes the colony's ordinary rhythms cracking. Emotional beat: wonder shading into unease.

chapters.title: Contested Orbit
chapters.summary: Juniper takes a routine cargo run past the derelict first-generation vessel Halcyon, claimed by both the Foundry Compact and the Verdance Assembly. His sensors pick up a carrier wave matching the frequency the children hum. He deletes the log. Emotional beat: fear disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: What the Dream Says
chapters.summary: Odile interviews the children; nine-year-old Tam describes a woman made of light singing instructions: 'Find the one who carries her name.' Odile cross-references colony records and finds only one Underhill. Emotional beat: the first thread pulled from a knot that won't hold.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Small Lies
chapters.summary: Flashback-heavy chapter: Juniper's arrival on Meridian ten years ago, the forged credentials, the insurance investigator's skill for making things disappear — including his own family name. We learn his mother was Ilsa Underhill, the Halcyon's architect, officially lost in transit. Emotional beat: guilt worn smooth by repetition.

chapters.title: The Compact Comes Asking
chapters.summary: A Foundry Compact intelligence officer, Sef Marrow, interviews Juniper about the anomaly near the Halcyon, probing whether he's a Verdance asset. Juniper's investigator instincts let him survive the interrogation, but Marrow leaves a card: 'When you're ready to talk about your mother.' Emotional beat: hunted.

chapters.title: Quarantine of Dreams
chapters.summary: The colony council, split between Compact and Assembly factions, votes to isolate the affected children 'for their safety.' Odile defies the order, recording their synchronized drawings — maps of the Halcyon's interior no living colonist has seen. Emotional beat: conscience over compliance.

chapters.title: The Message in the Hold
chapters.summary: Juniper discovers a sealed data core hidden in his own cargo bay — planted years ago by his mother before her death, keyed to his biometrics. It contains a partial message and a countdown synced to the children's dream cycle. Emotional beat: the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: Sef Marrow's War
chapters.summary: Marrow's POV reveals the Compact knows the dream originates from the Halcyon and plans to seize it and suppress the signal before the Assembly learns its contents. We see the war's machinery up close: fleets mobilizing over a story neither side wants told. Emotional beat: chilling institutional logic.

chapters.title: The Song Gets Louder
chapters.summary: The dream spreads to adults. Dockworkers walk off shifts; two crews refuse to arm patrol ships. Odile realizes the signal isn't controlling anyone — it's reminding them of something they already know. Emotional beat: collective awakening, terrifying and beautiful.

chapters.title: What Ilsa Built
chapters.summary: Juniper decodes the core's first layer: his mother's account of the founding fraud — both factions' land claims rest on records she falsified to prevent a first war. She hid the truth inside the Halcyon's systems, hoping a future generation could bear it. Emotional beat: inheritance as burden.

chapters.title: Bargaining with Ghosts
chapters.summary: Juniper approaches Marrow offering the core in exchange for safe passage to the Halcyon, while secretly contacting Odile through the children's network — they can hear him now when he sleeps. Emotional beat: a double agent against his own caution.

chapters.title: The Fleet at the Door
chapters.summary: Compact warships arrive at Meridian demanding the colony surrender the 'signal source.' The Assembly answers by dispatching its own fleet. Odile, elected spokesperson by the dreaming children, addresses both councils with the drawings. Emotional beat: courage without a plan.

chapters.title: Marrow's Doubt
chapters.summary: Marrow, ordered to prepare an assault on the colony, reviews Juniper's old insurance files and finds the pattern of erasures — and recognizes a man protecting something worth protecting. He delays the strike by six hours, gambling his career. Emotional beat: the enemy choosing conscience.

chapters.title: Running the Gap
chapters.summary: Juniper makes a desperate solo run through the contested corridor to the Halcyon, pursued by Compact interceptors and shadowed by an Assembly scout. The children, dreaming in unison, guide him through debris fields no chart shows. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into trust.

chapters.title: Aboard the Halcyon
chapters.summary: Inside the derelict, Juniper finds his mother's preserved consciousness interface — she recorded herself knowing someone would come. She tells him the full truth, including his own role in her death's cover-up, and asks him to choose freely whether to broadcast. Emotional beat: reckoning with the self.

chapters.title: Both Fleets Open Fire
chapters.summary: The six hours expire. Compact and Assembly squadrons engage above Meridian; the colony's shields fail section by section. Odile leads the children to the transmitter array, buying time by broadcasting the dream openly to every ship — freezing both fleets mid-volley. Emotional beat: defiance at the brink.

chapters.title: The Choice
chapters.summary: Juniper holds the broadcast key. His mother warns him the truth will delegitimize both governments and could shatter the colony instead of saving it. He thinks of ten years of invisibility and chooses visibility: he adds his own confession to hers. Emotional beat: the costliest honesty.

chapters.title: When the Echo Sings
chapters.summary: The full message — architect's confession and son's — plays across every fleet channel and colony screen. Weapons go silent. Grief moves through both armadas like weather. Marrow orders his ships to stand down before his superiors can countermand. Emotional beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Truth
chapters.summary: Neither government survives intact; a joint provisional council forms, with Odile and the children's testimony at its center. Some blame Juniper; more thank him. He expects to be exiled again and prepares to leave quietly. Emotional beat: bracing for old loneliness.

chapters.title: The One Who Carries Her Name
chapters.summary: Tam and the children find Juniper at the docking ring and ask him to stay — not as the invisible investigator but as Ilsa's son, the keeper of the story. He signs the crew manifest under his real name for the first time in ten years. Emotional beat: belonging accepted.

chapters.title: New Claims
chapters.summary: Months later, Juniper works claims again — but now as the colony's honest auditor of its own history, teaching children to read the records their founders falsified. The Halcyon becomes a memorial, open to both factions. The echo still sings, and everyone remembers why. Emotional beat: peace earned, not given.
